evidence: Failing-before run: `uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard_model.py -q -k 'waits or running'` gave 5 failed, 2 passed. The 2 passes were existing tests whose names contain "running". All 5 failures were AttributeError on TaskRow.waits_on or running_since. After the change, the same command gave 7 passed. Full run: `uv run --with textual --with pytest --with pytest-xdist python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard_model.py tests/test_dashboard_app.py -q -n 4` gave 210 passed. dashboard-status on the real store took 0.38s / 0.37s / 0.38s before and 0.43s / 0.37s / 0.39s after, against a 2s timeout. A read-only load_snapshot on the real store shows correct values: task-row-cells waits_on ('task-row-model',), verify-task-rows-phase waits_on ('task-row-cells', 'activity-failures'), and the two running tasks have running_since 2026-10-02 01:21:42+00:00.
observations: In scripts/dashboard_model.py, project:work-item is now in FULL_TYPES, so every work-item listing through _list uses --full and returns relationships.depends_on. TaskRow gains two fields with defaults: waits_on (a tuple, default ()) and running_since (datetime | None, default None). _task_rows(records, assignments=None) maps depends_on ids to records in the same list and keeps the slugs of dependencies whose lifecycle_state is not done, in depends_on order. running_since is the latest recorded_at among assignments whose payload.work_item matches the task id or slug, and is set only when the status is running. load_snapshot passes the assignments it already lists, so it makes no extra CLI call. load_phase_detail gets waits_on because it uses _list, but its running_since stays None because it passes no assignments. load_task_detail uses a plain list, so its waits_on stays empty; it uses those rows only for depends_on/blocks links, so nothing changes there. Five tests are added to tests/test_dashboard_model.py. The app is unchanged, and ActivityItem/_activity are untouched.
verdict: pass
claim: waits_on looks up dependencies only within the same effort's work-items, so a cross-effort dependency is dropped. A withdrawn dependency counts as "not done" and shows in waits_on, as the spec says literally. Change this if withdrawn dependencies should count as satisfied.
